intended_object: The canonical isometry of finite quadratic modules D(P_m(C)) ≅ C⊥/C. It goes from the discriminant quadratic module of the even Construction A lattice P_m(C) to the quadratic orthogonal quotient of the isotropic code C in (ℤ/m)^ι (m even, half-norm convention), and sends the class of a dual lattice vector to the class of its reduction mod m. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Nikulin Prop. 1.4.1, Ebeling, Conway–Sloane).
explanation: The definition composes three isometries. First, the equality of P_m(C) with the overlattice of L₀ = mℤ^ι glued along the transported copy of C. Second, the general isometry A_{L_H} ≅ H⊥/H for even overlattices glued along an isotropic subgroup. Third, the coordinate isometry A_{L₀} ≅ (ℤ/m)^ι, transported to orthogonal quotients. The companion theorem `discriminantOrthogonalQuotientIsometry_mk_intCast` shows the result is the canonical map: the class of an integer vector z of the dual lattice goes to the class of z mod m. This is exactly the textbook isomorphism. The hypotheses are the natural ones. The form x·x/(2m) mod 1 on (ℤ/m)^ι is only well defined for even m. Quadratic isotropy of C is equivalent to P_m(C) being even, which the discriminant quadratic module requires. Finite ι is the standard Construction A setting. The bilinear version for general m is a separate definition in the same file. Mathlib has no theory of lattice discriminant forms or Construction A, so there is no counterpart.
